rationale: B wins because it keeps the sellable stories tight and evidence-hungry: "Allbirds shrinks its way to a first margin gain, but the losses haven't stopped" is a real finance angle with a real margin-causality question. A has strong bones, especially "Allbirds is closing its own stores and signing a wholesale deal in the same breath," but it also wanders into "DTC brands are shrinking to survive" without the facts to earn that trend frame. That's speculation wearing a trade-story jacket.
gaps_in_A: "DTC brands are shrinking to survive" asserts a category trend with no comparable DTC evidence in the update; the proof list quietly admits it still needs that evidence.
"swaps wool for a sugarcane blend" misstates the material story; the update says a sugarcane-and-wool blend, not a clean swap away from wool.
"will finally make its shoes last" smuggles in an unproven prior durability failure. The facts only support Allbirds' own claim that the new blend is more durable than the original wool runner.
The DTC trend angle pads the set. Finance, channel tension, and product durability are the three cleaner stories.
gaps_in_B: "shelf space" and "floor space" assume physical in-store placement; the update only says a named retail wholesale partnership exists.
"shrinks its way to a first margin gain" flirts with causality before the margin bridge proves cuts caused the improvement, though the proof list mostly catches itself.
"This is the only angle... aimed at a trade desk" is sloppy because the product angle also targets materials trade outlets.
The next step jumps to "journalist-fit-check" before a named journalist exists; the cleaner immediate move is margin-proof gathering, then list-building.
